messages:
alex: quick sanity-check request — ran a throttling sim for APAC region for next quarter. with predicted peak arrival 420 rps, mean service time 0.035s (gpu-steady), and 18% cold-cache penalty, p95 looks fine but p99 creeps to ~620ms. thinking about adding admission control to keep p99 < 500ms. any obvious holes?
jamie: do you have the arrival distribution? is 420 rps sustained or spiky bursts? also what batch sizing are you assuming?
alex: modelled as Poisson with short bursts (peak windows of ~10m every hour). batching avg 6 tokens per request -> effective service time accounts for batching. used simple M/G/c approx for quick calc.
sam: rough check — if service time mean = 0.035 and cv~1.2 because of cold starts, the tail can blow up under utilization > 0.75. what's current fleet size/gpu hours planned?
alex: plan uses 28 A100-equivalent GPUs in APAC reserved pool (ongoing commit). that's ~672 GPU-hours/day capacity target for useful inference ops after overhead. we target util ~65% to keep headroom but seasonal peak growth pushes util to ~82% in our sim.
rachel: for admission control, we should be explicit: block when estimated queue depth would push expected p99 > 500ms, not just based on util. simple threshold on inflight + queued requests per shard is better.
jamie: agree. can we implement a fast estimator at edge: est_service = baseline + cold_prob * cold_penalty + batching_overhead; est_tail = est_service * tail_multiplier(0.95->1.8, 0.99->3.2) and deny if (inflight + queued) * est_tail / num_workers > p99_budget?
sam: that's reasonable. sample numbers: est_service=0.035 + 0.18*0.09(cold_penalty)=0.0512. tail_multiplier for p99 3.2 => est_tail ~0.163s. with 420 rps => average concurrency ~420*0.0512=21.5. if we hit bursts + queued -> concurrency can jump to 60-90 which gives p99 > 500ms. admission threshold around concurrency 30-35 for target p99 0.5s.
alex: thanks — that gives a simple knob. two followups: 1) how to convert that to GPU-hours impact for customers if we throttle (i.e., lost throughput)? 2) any suggestions for regional fallback policy?
rachel: 1) lost throughput = avg_block_rate * avg_tokens_per_req * token_cost_to_gpu_hour. we can estimate blocked rps during peak windows and map to delta GPU-hours across the quarter (include seasonal factor). 2) fallback: route excess to other region if network RTT < 80ms and legal/TOS allows; otherwise queue with backoff + 429 with Retry-After header and hint to client about expected retry window.
jamie: I'll prototype the estimator as a Lua filter for the edge LB today. keep it lightweight — just a few arithmetic ops + cached cold_prob per model. infra-bot: deploy-check: edge cluster capacity ok for adding filter (no rolling restarts needed).
alex: awesome. if prototype looks good, we should run a 48h canary in lower traffic zone and measure observed p95/p99 before full rollout. posting sim snippet for reference:
```
// pseudocode: concurrency_est = inflight + queued
est_service = 0.035 + cold_prob*0.09
est_tail = est_service * 3.2  // p99 multiplier
expected_p99 = (concurrency_est / workers) * est_tail
if expected_p99 > 0.5: reject_with_429()
```

sam: looks good. one caveat: this doesn't account for kernel contention when multiple tenants use same GPU; add tenant_scaling_factor if shared. also include network serialization when sending to remote region.
alex: good call. we'll add tenant factor and remote-penalty. thanks all — will follow up with canary metrics tomorrow. :rocket:
